label: No intellect that is not INFINITE_1 comprehends an INFINITE_1 being
paraphrase: Open bridge, analyst formulation, unattributed. For every g and x: if g is INFINITE_1, x has intellect (HAS_INTELLECT_1) and x is not INFINITE_1, then x does not comprehend g (Comprehends, the primitive relation of definition 4afe4ab4: knowing as perfectly as knowable). After ST I q.12 a.7: God is infinitely knowable, being infinite act, and no created intellect knows him infinitely, since its power of knowing, even raised by the light of glory, is finite. The bridge reads 'finite intellect' as an intellect whose being is not INFINITE_1, so it also carries the step from finite being to finite power of knowing. It says nothing about whether such an intellect knows g truly (q.12 a.7 ad 1: the blessed attain God without comprehending him) and nothing about g's knowing itself. Lead, not an objection: finite minds grasp quantitative infinities through finite principles (a definition fixes the natural numbers); its relevance to INFINITE_1 (unlimited act) is not shown, and it is weaker than it looks, since incompleteness cuts toward finite minds not knowing the natural numbers as perfectly as they are knowable. Control part 4: without it, a being with the nine can be comprehended by a caused intellect and is not INCOMPREHENSIBLE_2.
